title: Observer

act2.summary: a fifth, unforeseen consumer that can subscribe and unsubscribe at runtime, and one that throws without taking the others down

solutions.title: Built-in consumers as observers, behind one notify loop
solutions.tradeoff: Every consumer speaks one method (onAlert) instead of its own domain-flavored name (record/page/respond/append), and a new consumer can attach at runtime instead of being a name in the center's own file. The price: reading 'what does publishing an alert actually do' now means finding the loop and then finding every subscriber, instead of reading four lines top to bottom.

reviewFocus: Does subscribe()/unsubscribe() touch anything about the four built-in consumers, or do they keep working exactly as they did in act 1?
Is the try/catch around the loop doing anything besides swallowing the error - should a broken observer be logged or reported anywhere, or is silent containment the right call here?
Would unsubscribe() misbehave if the same observer were subscribed twice (indexOf + splice only removes the first occurrence) - and does any test actually cover that?
Is the walkthrough honest about why DomeGuard ignoring seeing alerts is a decision the consumer makes for itself, not something the center decides on its behalf?
Does the git log show subscribe/unsubscribe and the try/catch landing as one focused step, or mixed in with unrelated cleanup?
